root_cause.text: The q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare() function in the Qualcomm ASoC q6apm LPASS DAI playback path was not idempotent and reopened a DSP graph on repeated prepare calls without checking whether dai_data->graph[dai->id] was already initialized, causing leaked graph allocations.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “prepare can be called multiple times” and that this caused “multiple graph opens for playback path” resulting in “memory leaks,” and the patch fixes it by changing the playback condition from `if (substream->stream == SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_PLAYBACK)` to `if (substream->stream == SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_PLAYBACK && dai_data->graph[dai->id] == NULL)`, adding the missing existing-graph check before `q6apm_graph_open()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null-check so the playback graph is opened only once per DAI instead of reopening an existing graph.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the playback path in q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare() was changed from checking only whether substream->stream equals SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_PLAYBACK to additionally requiring dai_data->graph[dai->id] == NULL before calling q6apm_graph_open().
intent_record.how: At runtime, playback graph creation now happens only when no graph is already stored for the given DAI ID, preventing repeated or duplicate q6apm_graph_open() calls for an existing playback graph and avoiding unnecessary reinitialization or resource misuse.

grouping_result.intent: Add a null-check so the playback graph is opened only once per DAI instead of reopening an existing graph.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by checking whether the playback graph is already initialized before opening it again, making repeated prepare calls idempotent and preventing leaked graph allocations.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally opens a new playback DSP graph on every prepare call. Without checking whether dai_data->graph[dai->id] is already initialized, repeated prepare calls reopen the graph and leak the previous allocation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally opens a new playback DSP graph during prepare. Because q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare() did not first check whether dai_data->graph[dai->id] was already initialized, repeated prepare calls reopened the graph and leaked the previously allocated graph object.

commit 30ad723b93ade607a678698e5947a55a4375c3a1
Author: Srinivas Kandagatla <srini@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Oct 26 12:16:53 2021 +0100

    ASoC: qdsp6: audioreach: add q6apm lpass dai support
    
    Add support to Audio port dais on LPASS Audio IP using
    existing common q6dsp-lpass-ports.
    
    Signed-off-by: Srinivas Kandagatla <srinivas.kandagatla@linaro.org>
    Reviewed-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211026111655.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the prepare-path graph open logic and the absence of any guard for repeated calls. In `q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare()`, for playback it unconditionally does `graph = q6apm_graph_open(dai->dev, NULL, dai->dev, graph_id);` inside `if (substream->stream == SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_PLAYBACK) { ... }` and then immediately stores it with `dai_data->graph[graph_id] = graph;`. There is no check such as whether `dai_data->graph[dai->id]` is already non-NULL/already initialized before reopening. Since ALSA prepare can be called multiple times, this makes the function non-idempotent for playback and can overwrite the existing graph pointer, leaking the previously opened graph allocation. The rest of the function continues using `dai_data->graph[dai->id]` for `q6apm_graph_media_format_pcm(...)`, `q6apm_graph_prepare(...)`, and `q6apm_graph_start(...)`, but nowhere prevents a second open on repeated prepare. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix (guarding against reopening an already initialized graph / making prepare idempotent) is not present.
